dish: Asahikawa shinkoyaki — charcoal-grilled young half-chicken in secret tare (¥1,045)
n: Dokushaku Sanshirō, Asahikawa (独酌 三四郎)
w: A 1946 izakaya ten minutes from Asahikawa Station: shinkoyaki under the house tare and sake chosen by the proprietress — the stop in Kodoku no Gurume's 2016 Asahikawa New Year special.

dish: Biei ebi-don (fried-prawn rice bowl) and the original 'Jun-dog'
n: Yōshoku to Café Junpei, Biei (洋食とcafé じゅんぺい)
address: Honchō 4-chōme, Biei, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: An 8-minute walk from Biei Station: the town's famous prawn-tempura bowl, tails sticking out over the rim, and the birthplace of the rice-wrapped fried-prawn 'Jun-dog'. Lunch only, until sold out.

dish: Furano omu-curry, Furano-wagyu dishes and local-milk cheese tofu
w: A rustic Furano Station-side local-food house opened during the filming of 'Kita no Kuni kara' — Furano beef, wild-vegetable and seafood dishes, and listed by the tourism body for Furano omu-curry.

dish: Furano melon — fully-ripened melon by the slice, melon soft-serve and melon sweets
n: Tomita Melon House, Nakafurano (とみたメロンハウス)
address: Miya-machi 3-32, Nakafurano, Sorachi District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: A melon grower's shop and deck café facing the Tokachi range, near the lavender farms — cut Furano melon, melon soft-serve and melon-only sweets. Summer season only (Jun–Sep).

dish: additive-free, water-free jams (38 kinds) from Furano fruit and vegetables
n: Furano Jam-en, Rokugō (ふらのジャム園)
w: A jam workshop since 1974 in Rokugō, the 'Kita no Kuni kara' valley 30 minutes from Furano — jams cooked with no added water; free entry and tastings, with the Rokugō lookout beside it.

dish: junmai sake from Daisetsu groundwater — a 140-year-old Gifu brewery relocated to Higashikawa in 2020
address: Nishi 2-gō Kita 23, Higashikawa, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Japan's rare town-built, privately-run sake brewery: Michizakura (founded 1877 in Nakatsugawa, Gifu) moved its whole operation and its tōji to Higashikawa for the cold and the Taisetsu spring water. Shop 10:00–15:30.

dish: raclette and the Euro-award-winning white-mould 'Sasayuki' from Brown Swiss milk
n: Kyōdō Gakusha Shintoku Farm (共働学舎新得農場)
w: A farming community at the foot of the Hidaka range making European-style farmhouse cheese by hand from grass-fed Brown Swiss cows — its white-mould Sasayuki has taken medals in European contests; farm shop on site.

dish: Tokachi farm produce, butadon and local sweets under one roof at the ban'ei track
w: Tokachi's food showcase inside the Obihiro Racecourse grounds: a farmers' direct market, eateries and sweet shops cooking local ingredients, specialty coffee and the horse museum — pair it with an evening of ban'ei racing.

dish: Tokachi butadon and bread from Otofuke wheat (Japan's top wheat town)
n: Michi-no-eki Otofuke Natsuzora no Furusato (道の駅 おとふけ なつぞらのふる里)
w: Rebuilt and reopened in April 2022 as one of Hokkaido's biggest roadside stations, with a 'Natsuzora' (NHK drama) zone and a food court of Tokachi soul food — butadon, local-wheat bakeries and dairy.

dish: Asahikawa shōyu ramen and the 'horumon ramen' topped with grilled pork offal
n: Rāmen Senmon Himawari, Asahikawa (ラーメン専門 ひまわり 大雪通店)
address: Taisetsu-dōri 3-chōme, Tokuichi Bldg 1F, Asahikawa, Hokkaido, Japan
w: An old-guard Asahikawa shop 10 minutes' walk from Shin-Asahikawa Station that has fed generations of students — classic lard-sealed shōyu, and its signature bowl crowned with thick-cut grilled pork offal. Lunch to 17:00.

dish: Tsuboya's Asahikawa sweets — the 'kibana' almond-cookie line made in the on-site factory — and cake at Café Bunran
n: Tsuboya Kibana no Mori, Asahikawa (壺屋 き花の杜)
w: Asahikawa's century-old confectioner Tsuboya in a brick-and-timber shop set in a 1,000-tsubo garden: its standards and shop-only sweets, a viewable kibana production line, and the Café Bunran tea room.

dish: 'Furano mochi' — Rokkatei's Furano-only sweet of local salted peas — in a glass tea room over the vineyards
n: Campana Rokkatei, Furano (カンパーナ六花亭)
w: Rokkatei's Furano store on Shimizuyama: a glass hall in 24,000 tsubo of vines with the Furano basin and Daisetsu range beyond; the tea room serves the shop-exclusive Furano mochi.

dish: Obihiro butadon — Hokkaido pork grilled slice by slice in Hageten's pre-war tare, over Koshihikari
n: Butadon no Butahage, Obihiro Station (豚丼のぶたはげ 帯広本店)
address: Esta Obihiro West Wing 1F, Nishi 2-jō Minami 12-chōme, Obihiro, Hokkaido, Japan
w: The station-side butadon specialist spun off from the old tempura house Hageten (whose butadon got too popular) — 15 seats plus butadon bentō to take on the train.

dish: milk jam — farm milk and Hokkaido sugar only — on waffles in the pasture tea room
n: Tokachi Shinmura Bokujō, Kamishihoro (十勝しんむら牧場)
w: A grazing dairy north of Obihiro famous across Japan for its milk jam; the farm's tea room serves it on waffles and soft-serve. Open Apr–Dec.
